source_caption:
The Ritual turns a simple hiking trip into a slow descent into grief, fear, and psychological horror. Directed by David Bruckner and based on the novel by Adam Nevill, the film follows four friends traveling through the forests of Sweden after the tragic death of one of their close friends.

What makes the film so effective is how grounded the characters feel. The tension doesn’t come only from the creature hiding in the woods, but from guilt, unresolved trauma, and the growing paranoia between the group. The forest itself becomes suffocating, filled with strange symbols, abandoned cabins, and an atmosphere that constantly feels wrong even before the horror fully reveals itself.

Unlike many modern horror films that rely heavily on jump scares, The Ritual builds dread slowly through silence, isolation, and psychological pressure. When the creature finally appears, it stands out as one of the most memorable monster designs in recent horror, inspired by Norse mythology and revealed just enough to remain unsettling.

At its core, the film is really about survivor’s guilt and cowardice. Beneath the supernatural horror, it’s a story about men struggling with trauma and the fear of confronting who they truly are when stripped of comfort and safety.

source_details.synopsis: The Ritual is a 2025 American horror film directed by David Midell and written by Midell and Enrico Natale. Based on a true story, it follows priests Theophilus Riesinger (Al Pacino) and Joseph Steiger (Dan Stevens) as they attempt to put aside their differences to save an allegedly possessed young woman Emma Schmidt (Abigail Cowen) through a series of exorcisms. The film was released by XYZ Films on June 6, 2025, and received generally negative reviews from critics.
